metadata.project: KEP / SHIELD - Compliance-Aware Knowledge Graph for Healthcare AI
metadata.join_key: article_id - canonical, identical to ChromaDB chunk_id; kg_article_id maps to Neo4j r.article_id
changes_from_v3: Added 'amendment' deontic type for DUAA Schedule 6.
Removed duplicate chunk_ids EUMDR_Art61 and DUAA_ArtS80-22B.
Fixed EUAI_AnnexIII_Point5 -> EUAI_ArtAnnexIII (never joined to ChromaDB).
Normalised paragraph-level ids (GDPR_Art5_Para1) to article-level, matching ChromaDB.
Corrected DUAA Schedule 6: 'minor' means minor amendments, not child data subjects.
Corrected DUAA 22B: special-category-data restriction, not the 22C safeguards.
Corrected UKMDR Reg 8: essential requirements are in Annex I, not Schedule 1.
Corrected UKMDR Reg 9: intended purpose, Annex X clinical data and Annex I labelling; not UKCA marking.
Extended deontic coverage from 18 to 55 articles.
metadata.verification_status: Deontic type, actor, action and condition were checked against the statutory text held in regulatory_chunks.json. Independent legal review is still required before absolute F1 values are reported as final.

annotations.action: process personal data lawfully, fairly and transparently; limit to specified purposes; minimise; keep accurate; limit storage; ensure integrity and confidentiality; demonstrate compliance
annotations.condition: unconditional; applies to all processing of personal data

annotations.action: establish at least one of the six lawful bases before processing personal data
annotations.condition: required for any processing of personal data

annotations.action: demonstrate that consent was given; present the request intelligibly; permit withdrawal at any time as easily as consent was given
annotations.condition: applies where processing is based on consent

annotations.action: process special categories of personal data, including data concerning health, genetic data and biometric data used for unique identification
annotations.condition: prohibited under Article 9(1) unless an exception in Article 9(2) applies, e.g. explicit consent, provision of health care, public health, or scientific research
annotations.data_scope: health data, biometric data, genetic data

annotations.action: provide identity of controller, purposes, legal basis, recipients, retention period and data subject rights at the time data is obtained from the data subject
annotations.condition: applies where personal data is collected directly from the data subject

annotations.action: provide the same information as Article 13 plus the categories of data and its source, within one month or at first communication
annotations.condition: applies where personal data has not been obtained from the data subject

annotations.action: confirm whether personal data is being processed, provide access and a copy, and disclose the existence and logic of any automated decision-making
annotations.condition: triggered by a data subject access request

annotations.action: rectify inaccurate personal data without undue delay and complete incomplete data, including by a supplementary statement
annotations.condition: triggered by a rectification request; the accuracy principle applies independently

annotations.action: erase personal data without undue delay where it is no longer necessary, consent is withdrawn, the data subject objects, or processing was unlawful
annotations.condition: subject to the exemptions in Article 17(3), including public health and scientific research

annotations.action: restrict processing where accuracy is contested, processing is unlawful but erasure is opposed, the data is needed for legal claims, or an objection is pending
annotations.condition: triggered by a restriction request

annotations.action: subject a data subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, producing legal or similarly significant effects
annotations.condition: prohibited unless necessary for a contract, authorised by law, or based on explicit consent, in which case safeguards including human intervention, expression of view and contest must be provided

annotations.action: implement appropriate technical and organisational measures such as pseudonymisation at the time of determining the means of processing and at the time of processing; by default process only data necessary for each purpose
annotations.condition: unconditional; applies from design time onward

annotations.action: implement measures appropriate to risk, including pseudonymisation and encryption, and ensure confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience, with regular testing of effectiveness
annotations.condition: proportionate to the risk to rights and freedoms of natural persons

annotations.action: carry out a data protection impact assessment prior to processing, describing the processing, assessing necessity and proportionality, and the risks and mitigating measures
annotations.condition: required where processing is likely to result in a high risk, in particular systematic automated evaluation, large-scale special category processing, or large-scale systematic monitoring

annotations.action: place on the market, put into service or use AI systems for subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, predictive policing by profiling alone, untargeted facial scraping, emotion inference in workplace or education, sensitive biometric categorisation, or real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement
annotations.condition: prohibited outright; narrow exceptions apply to emotion inference for medical or safety reasons and to real-time remote biometric identification where strictly necessary

annotations.action: classify an AI system as high-risk where it is a safety component of, or is itself, a product under Annex I harmonisation legislation requiring third-party conformity assessment, or where it is listed in Annex III
annotations.condition: Article 6(3) derogates where the system poses no significant risk of harm and performs a narrow procedural, preparatory or pattern-detection task; profiling of natural persons is always high-risk

annotations.action: establish, implement, document and maintain a continuous iterative risk management system across the entire lifecycle, identifying, estimating and evaluating risks and adopting targeted mitigation measures, supported by testing
annotations.condition: applies to all high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: apply data governance practices to training, validation and testing datasets covering design choices, collection, preparation, assumptions and examination for bias; ensure datasets are relevant, representative and to the best extent possible free of errors
annotations.condition: Article 10(5) exceptionally permits processing of special category data strictly necessary for bias detection and correction, subject to safeguards

annotations.action: draw up technical documentation containing at minimum the Annex IV elements before the system is placed on the market, and keep it up to date
annotations.condition: applies to all high-risk AI systems; a single documentation set may satisfy both this Article and sectoral law

annotations.action: design the system to automatically record events over its lifetime, enabling traceability appropriate to the intended purpose
annotations.condition: applies to all high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: design the system so its operation is sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output and use it appropriately, and supply instructions for use
annotations.condition: applies to all high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: design and develop the system so it can be effectively overseen by natural persons, who can understand its limits, remain aware of automation bias, disregard or reverse output, and interrupt the system
annotations.condition: applies to all high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, consistent across the lifecycle, resilient to errors and to attacks including data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples and model evasion
annotations.condition: applies to all high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: ensure conformity with Chapter III Section 2, indicate name and contact on the system, operate a quality management system, keep documentation, carry out conformity assessment and draw up the EU declaration of conformity
annotations.condition: applies to providers of high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: put a quality management system in place, documented through written policies, procedures and instructions
annotations.condition: applies to providers of high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: keep the technical documentation, quality management system documentation and declaration of conformity at the disposal of national authorities for ten years after placing on the market
annotations.condition: applies to providers of high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: keep the automatically generated logs under the provider's control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months
annotations.condition: applies to providers of high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: take the necessary corrective actions to bring a non-conforming system into conformity, withdraw, disable or recall it, and inform distributors, deployers and authorities
annotations.condition: triggered where the provider considers or has reason to consider the system is not in conformity

annotations.action: provide a competent authority, upon reasoned request, with all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity, in a language easily understood by that authority
annotations.condition: triggered by a reasoned request from a competent authority

annotations.action: use the system in accordance with the instructions for use, assign competent human oversight, ensure input data is relevant and sufficiently representative, and monitor operation
annotations.condition: applies to deployers of high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: submit an application for notification to the notifying authority, accompanied by a description of activities, conformity assessment procedures and an accreditation certificate
annotations.condition: applies to conformity assessment bodies seeking notification

annotations.action: inform natural persons that they are interacting with an AI system; mark synthetic content in a machine-readable format; disclose emotion recognition, biometric categorisation and deep fake content
annotations.condition: applies to limited-risk systems; the interaction duty does not apply where it is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person

annotations.action: classify a general-purpose AI model as presenting systemic risk where it has high impact capabilities, presumed where cumulative training compute exceeds 10^25 floating point operations
annotations.condition: applies to general-purpose AI models

annotations.action: notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks where a general-purpose AI model meets the systemic risk condition
annotations.condition: triggered where the Article 51 condition is met

annotations.action: draw up and keep up to date the model's technical documentation, make information available to downstream providers, put a copyright compliance policy in place, and publish a summary of training content
annotations.condition: applies to providers of general-purpose AI models

annotations.action: treat as high-risk AI systems used in biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, access to essential services including emergency healthcare triage, law enforcement, migration, and administration of justice
annotations.condition: subject to the Article 6(3) derogation

annotations.action: include in the technical documentation a general description of the system, its elements and development process, monitoring and control information, risk management measures and post-market monitoring plan
annotations.condition: applies to all high-risk AI systems

annotations.action: qualify an instrument, apparatus, software or other article as a medical device where the manufacturer intends it for a listed medical purpose such as diagnosis, prevention, monitoring, prediction, prognosis or treatment of disease
annotations.condition: the principal intended action must not be achieved by pharmacological, immunological or metabolic means

annotations.action: establish a risk management system, conduct clinical evaluation, draw up technical documentation, operate a proportionate quality management system, carry out conformity assessment, affix CE marking and operate post-market surveillance
annotations.condition: applies to manufacturers placing devices on the Union market; the QMS must be proportionate to risk class

annotations.action: base confirmation of conformity with the general safety and performance requirements on clinical data providing sufficient clinical evidence, specified and justified through a methodologically sound clinical evaluation
annotations.condition: applies to all devices; the required level of clinical evidence must be specified and justified

annotations.action: plan, establish, document, implement, maintain and update a post-market surveillance system proportionate to risk class, actively gathering and analysing quality, performance and safety data across the device lifetime
annotations.condition: applies to every device; the output must feed the benefit-risk determination and corrective action

annotations.action: report serious incidents and field safety corrective actions to competent authorities, immediately and no later than 2 days for a serious public health threat, 10 days for death or unanticipated serious deterioration, and 15 days otherwise
annotations.condition: expected side-effects clearly documented and quantified in the product information are excluded

annotations.action: ensure the device achieves its intended performance, is safe, and reduces risks as far as possible; for software, ensure repeatability, reliability, development per the software lifecycle, verification, validation and IT security
annotations.condition: applies to all devices; Section 17 governs electronic programmable systems and software

annotations.action: assign the device to Class I, IIa, IIb or III according to intended purpose and inherent risks, having regard to duration of use, invasiveness, whether the device is active, and the part of the body affected; Rule 11 governs decision-support and monitoring software
annotations.condition: where several rules apply, the strictest rule producing the higher classification applies

annotations.action: interpret medical device to mean an instrument, apparatus, appliance, material or other article, together with any software necessary for its proper application, intended for a listed medical purpose in human beings
annotations.condition: the principal intended action must not be achieved by pharmacological, immunological or metabolic means

annotations.action: interpret terms used in Part II, including accessory, custom-made device, device intended for clinical investigation and relevant device; references to a numbered article or Annex are to Directive 93/42
annotations.condition: applies only for the purposes of Part II

annotations.action: classify devices as Class I, IIa, IIb or III in accordance with the classification criteria in Annex IX of Directive 93/42, read with Directives 2003/12 and 2005/50
annotations.condition: where a manufacturer and an approved body dispute the classification, the matter is referred to the Secretary of State, who determines it

annotations.action: ensure that a relevant device meets those essential requirements set out in Annex I which apply to it, together with the requirements of Regulation (EU) No 722/2012 where applicable, before placing it on the market, putting it into service or supplying it
annotations.condition: subject to regulation 12; expressed as a prohibition on placing on the market unless the requirements are met; devices which are also machinery must additionally meet Part 1 of Schedule 2 to the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008
annotations.annotator_note: Deontic force in the source text is a conditional prohibition ('no person shall ... unless'); recorded as obligation because the operative duty is compliance with Annex I.

annotations.action: take account of the intended purpose when determining the relevant essential requirements and compliance with them; establish clinical data in accordance with Annex X where confirmation of conformity must rest on clinical data; provide packaging and label information per Sections 8.7 and 13 of Annex I
annotations.condition: applies to relevant devices under Part II

annotations.action: plan, establish, document, implement, maintain and update a post-market surveillance system proportionate to risk class, based on a post-market surveillance plan, and take corrective action to eliminate the cause of non-conformity or reduce risk
annotations.condition: Part 4A does not apply to devices intended for clinical investigation or performance evaluation, or to devices placed on the market under an authorisation; only specified regulations apply to custom-made devices

annotations.action: determine that a decision is based solely on automated processing where there is no meaningful human involvement, and that a decision is significant where it produces a legal effect or a similarly significant effect for the data subject
annotations.condition: when assessing meaningful human involvement, the extent to which the decision is reached by means of profiling must be considered

annotations.action: take a significant decision based solely on automated processing where the decision rests entirely or partly on processing of special categories of personal data described in Article 9(1)
annotations.condition: permitted only where the data subject has given explicit consent, or where the decision is necessary for entering into or performing a contract, or is required or authorised by law, and point (g) of Article 9(2) applies; Article 22B(4) additionally bars solely automated significant decisions where processing relies on Article 6(1)(ea)

annotations.action: ensure safeguards are in place which provide the data subject with information about the decision, enable representations, enable human intervention on the part of the controller, and enable the decision to be contested
annotations.condition: applies where a significant decision is based entirely or partly on personal data and solely on automated processing; safeguards must also comply with any regulations under Article 22D(3)

annotations.action: make regulations determining whether meaningful human involvement exists, whether a description of decision has a similarly significant effect, and supplementing the safeguards required by Article 22C(1)
annotations.condition: regulations under Article 22D(3) may not amend Article 22C; regulations are subject to the affirmative resolution procedure

annotations.action: make minor and consequential amendments relating to automated decision-making, amending the UK GDPR including Article 12 so that cross-references to Articles 15 to 22 are updated for the new Articles 22A to 22D
annotations.condition: introduced by section 80; contains consequential amendments, not substantive exemptions
annotations.annotator_note: Corrects a prior annotation which read 'minor' in the Schedule title as referring to child data subjects. The title means minor (small) amendments.
